column1: # tests/linux/runsweep_recipes.tsv — how to smoke test each user/*.ad, and what
# each one CLAIMS to do. Read by scripts/hamlinux_runsweep.sh.
#   class   filter  reads stdin, writes stdout
#           cmd     an ordinary command; argv and/or the filesystem
#           gui     needs /dev/wsys — a scene client or the toolkit
#           daemon  runs for ever by design; "still up at the timeout" is a PASS
#           hosttest a *_host.ad harness whose job is to self-test
#           filter/cmd/gui/daemon/hosttest are RUN. The rest are not:
#           disk    wants a block device, a partition table or an image
#           net     wants a host on the outside; the sweep stays offline
#           payload runs as /init or as a bare-metal EL0 image, not as a program
#           unsafe  would reboot, halt or replace PID 1
#   argv    argv to run it with. %F %F2 are scratch text files, %D a scratch
#           directory, %NEW a path that does NOT exist.
#   stdin   `-` for immediate EOF, `%F` for the scratch file, else a literal
#   claim   what the program says IT does, in its own header — including where
#           it deliberately differs from POSIX. THIS IS THE ORACLE. `wc` and
#           `head` here are stdin-only and ignore file operands; judging them
#           against GNU manufactures failures out of correct programs
